messages:
maya: Heads-up — after yesterday's binpack tweak I'm seeing p99 gRPC latencies spike for multi-GPU inference jobs in us-west1. Grafana shows short bursts where top-of-rack NIC goes to 100% and we get packet drops.

maya: Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/inf; p99 jumps from ~60ms -> 400ms for a few mins.

maya: quick kernel qdisc dump (cropped):
```
root@node-42:~# tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc pfifo_fast 0: rate 0bit
 Sent 12345 bytes  pkts 120 drops 18 overlimits 0
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
```

liam: Are these jobs using NVLink (intra-node) or sharding across nodes? can you paste the pod spec?

maya: They request 2 GPUs and end up spread across two siblings in same rack (we pack for GPU count). Pod snippet: 
```yaml
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: "2"
annotations:
  inference/expected-bw: "500mbps" # best-effort from user
```
No hostNetwork, no explicit topologySpread.

nora: My hunch: scheduler is aggressively binpacking GPUs across nodes in the same rack which saturates the ToR uplink when multiple concurrent jobs start. NVLink wouldn't cause NIC drops; this is host NIC congestion. We should prefer rack-local full-node placements (both gpus on same host) when model does heavy inter-node comms, or limit rack-level density.

sam: We currently treat only gpu=count + cpu+mem for fit. Proposal: introduce a "net.bandwidth" scalar resource to the scheduler and admission controller. Jobs declare expected bandwidth (or we infer from model tag). Scheduler predicate pseudo: 
```go
// pseudo-predicate
if node.AvailableNet < pod.Request.Net { reject }
if rack.UsedNet + pod.Request.Net > rack.Capacity*0.8 { deprioritize }
```
This lets us avoid packing many high-IO pods onto same rack.

sam: Implementation plan: 1) add pod annotation parsing (inference/expected-bw) 2) expose node.netCapacity via kubelet metric 3) scheduler plugin to score by rack headroom 4) small canary rollout.

maya: Sounds good. What about cost? reserving 20% headroom reduces utilization — how do we quantify tradeoff vs SLAs?

sam: Quick back-of-envelope: if a rack has 10Gbps ToR and we reserve 20% (2Gbps) that's 2Gbps * 3600s * 24 = ~207GB/day unused capacity per rack. If that prevents 1-2 degraded inference runs per day (SLA penalties or customer impact), it's worth it. We should run canary to measure actual degradation incidence before broad reservation.

devops-bot: canary-scheduler-patch v2 deployed to us-west1 (10% of scheduling decisions). Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/patches/1234

maya: I'll attach a sampling job and collect p50/p95/p99 for next 6 hours. Ping eng-sre if p99 > 200ms or ToR drops > 5 in a minute. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
